meta.name: Fitness tracker reviews
meta.description: IronLog, SetCount and LiftLab. The flagship demo.

defaultContext.product: IronLog is a paid workout tracker for strength athletes on iOS and Apple Watch. We're deciding what to fix before the next annual-pricing push.
defaultContext.decision: Which problems to fix before the next annual-pricing push.

items.text: Just started lifting and wanted a simple app.£79 a year is nuts when I can log sets for free elsewhere. The free version does barely anything—no charts, no syncing. Feels like paying for the whole product.

Rest timer is completely broken on the Watch. Lock my phone, step away between sets, and the notification never comes. I'm standing there guessing when to lift again. This defeats the whole point of wearing it.
The progress charts are incredible. I can actually see my volume trend over three months and spot where I hit a plateau on bench. Way better than just writing it down.

Great app and I like the program templates, but coming from Strong there's no way to import my two years of workouts. Had to leave all that history behind and start fresh. Shame because otherwise it's solid.
Watch rest timer stops the moment I turn my phone off or open Spotify. Defeated the purpose of having it on my wrist. Switched apps after two weeks.
Paid for the year and mostly happy, but my Watch keeps losing sets mid-session. I'll log three exercises, sync, and only two show up on my phone. Sometimes they arrive an hour later. Frustrating.
Missing tons of cable machine variations and Smith machine exercises. My gym has a ton of those, so I end up creating custom entries that clutter everything. Not ideal.
The Watch app connection drops constantly during my workouts. Lost an entire session last week because sets never synced to the phone. Unreliable.
Really solid tracker and I'm keeping my subscription. Rest timer does hiccup if I alt-tab to messages or music though. Wish it was more persistent, but it's a small nag.
Would love superset support. Right now I log them as separate blocks and the timer fires after every single exercise, so I'm constantly silencing notifications. Makes giant sets a pain.
Love the Pro tier. The plate calculator alone saves me mental math every session—tells me exactly which plates to load. Charts are great too and the price is fair for what you get.

Excellent app overall. Only wish the exercise library had more machine variants—pec deck, hack squat, some of the leg press styles at my gym aren't there. Otherwise I'd give it five stars without hesitation.
Works well for tracking. Would benefit from a way to push programs or share workout logs with my athletes so they can see what I want them to do instead of sending screenshots.
The interface is incredibly clean and the buttons are huge—logging with sweaty hands is so easy. Perfect for my first strength app.
Rest timer is useless. Soon as I put my phone down or another app pops up, it stops working. Defeats the purpose of having a timer if I have to keep the screen on.
Does exactly what it says. Best tracker I've used so far and super straightforward to set up.
Timer doesn't work in the background. I'll be resting between squats, phone locks, and I miss the notification. Defeats the whole point of paying for Pro.
Good app overall and I keep using it. Cable rows and some specialty machines from my gym are missing though, so I have to log them as custom exercises. Would be more complete with those.
Too many onboarding questions and goal quizzes before I could log my first set. Just wanted to start lifting, not fill out a survey. Skipped most of it.
The plate calculator is a game-changer for fast setup between sets, especially for barbell work. Eighty bucks a year and it pays for itself in saved time. Highly recommend.
Solid tracker. The one thing I'd add is a way to share training programs directly with my clients so they see live progress instead of me emailing spreadsheets.
Tracks workouts reliably. Would improve it by letting me push or share structured programs into the app for my athletes, rather than juggling screenshots and files.
Works well. Would appreciate a dark mode option—early morning workouts and the white screen is pretty bright on my Watch.
Sync between Watch and phone is broken. Sets logged on the Watch take forever to arrive or don't show up at all. Lost sets mid-session. Switched apps.
Does the job and I'm sticking with it. Simple, reliable logging.
Cancelled my Pro subscription. The free tier already logs sets just fine—paying 50 quid a year for charts and sync feels excessive when competitors do it cheaper or free.
The plate calculator is brilliant. My athletes see exactly what to load and there's no confusion between sets. Saves so much coaching time.
Really solid for program tracking. Wish I could import my Fitbod history when I switched over, but there's no import tool so I lost five years of data. App itself is great though.
Latest update made everything faster. Nice to see the team improving it.
Great to see kilogram labels throughout—makes tracking in my home gym cleaner. Appreciate the European support.

Paying 59 bucks a year for what amounts to a basic workout log is a joke. The free version does almost everything the paid tier does. Should be half the price or actually give us something worth the money. Switching back to Strong.

Love the plate math feature and charts, but the setup asked me to answer so many questions before I could log my first squat. Good news is once I got past all that, importing from Strong worked fine and I've been solid ever since.

Rest timer is absolutely useless on the Watch. I start it, lock my phone, and it either resets or stops notifying me halfway through my set. Defeats the whole purpose of having it on my wrist. Very frustrating.

My gym just got a new hack squat and the app doesn't have it in the library. Same problem with the belt squat and half the cable machines. Ended up creating custom entries that now clutter everything. Not acceptable for a paid tracker.
Rest timer in the background is hit or miss. Sometimes I'll put the phone down between bench sets and it never alerts me. Otherwise solid app and worth the subscription, but this needs to be fixed.
Solid.
The trend charts are fantastic. I can actually see my 1RM estimates climbing week to week and spot when I'm plateauing. Makes a real difference in how I plan the next block.
Good app overall but logging in a dark gym at 5am with the bright white screen is brutal. Would love a dark mode option that follows my phone's system setting.
Worth every penny. The structured program import and workout tracking beats anything I've tried, and the interface is clean. Renewed without thinking twice.
Switched from Hevy and there's no way to import my old workouts. Had to manually rebuild my history, which is annoying when you've been logging for years. CSV import would solve this.
The volume charts per muscle group have completely changed how I think about my programming. I can actually see if my back work is keeping up with my chest. Exactly what I needed.
I was worried 59 bucks was steep for a new app, but the program library and integration make it stick. I'm already saving time versus the spreadsheets I was using.
App works well for logging, but importing from JEFIT was impossible. Had to start from scratch. If they added a CSV importer this would be perfect.

The rest timer on my Watch is completely broken. Locks the phone for one set and it either disappears or goes off at random. Tried reinstalling and nothing changed. This is my main reason for using the Watch app.
The plate calculator is genius. Load up 315 and it instantly tells me which plates to grab per side. Saves me thinking between every single set. Best feature in any app I've used.
Seeing my actual strength curve on the charts is incredible. The 1RM graph shows me exactly where I'm weak and where I'm strong. Been using this data to completely overhaul my weak points.
Loved how fast I was logging sets. SetCount got me training in under a minute instead of fiddling with onboarding screens. My only wish is I'd found it sooner.
I share progress charts with my athletes to show them the data behind their programming decisions. The muscle group breakdown and volume trends make coaching conversations so much clearer.
Does everything I need. Logs sets on my Watch, syncs to the phone, shows me what I did last week. Best tracker I've used.
Support team got back to me in hours when I couldn't restore my purchase. Problem solved and didn't lose any data. Really appreciated the help.
IronLog is great for tracking, but the exercise library is missing so many cable variations and machine exercises. My commercial gym has equipment that just isn't in here. Wish they'd add them.
Best tracker out there. Clean design, works flawlessly on my Watch, and logging is painless.
Too much friction to get started. Onboarding was endless and I couldn't import my Fitbod history, so I rebuilt everything manually. Finally got going but it was frustrating at first.

Love the simplicity but I really need superset support. Right now I log each exercise separately and the rest timer pops off between every movement. For pairs and giant sets it's awkward. Otherwise excellent.

Logged a full upper body workout on the Watch at my gym this morning and half the sets never showed up on my phone. They arrived 20 minutes later, mixed in with duplicates. Lost the whole session's data essentially.
The plate calculator in SetCount Pro saved me so much mental math at the rack. Exactly what I needed and the price is fair for what you get.

Overall really solid app, but supersets are a pain. I have to log each exercise in its own block, which means the rest timer fires between every movement instead of letting me cycle through a pair. Needs circuit grouping.
Missing so many machines from the library. The pec deck, Smith machine, leg press variations—I'm creating custom entries for everything and my history is a mess. Frustrating for a paid tracker.

Great app and I'll keep paying for it, but the rest timer sometimes doesn't notify when the phone is locked. I have to manually check my watch or look at my phone. Not a dealbreaker but it's annoying.
Good overall but cable exercises are severely lacking. My gym setup relies on the cable machine and I have to make my own entries every week. More exercise variety would make this perfect.

I coach a dozen athletes and wanted to push programs to them via LiftLab, but there's no way to share or sync a program I write. We're stuck doing screenshots and copying stuff into spreadsheets. Makes it hard to keep everyone on the same plan.

Love the app overall, but the rest timer is a nightmare in the gym. Soon as I grab my water or check my phone for messages, the timer stops or resets. And I can't group exercises into supersets, so the timer goes off between every single movement. Defeats the purpose.
The charts here are fantastic. I can see my athletes' progress over weeks and months, estimated 1RMs, volume trends. Makes coaching decisions so much easier. This is why I renew every year.

Really solid app, but I've been using it at 5am in a dark gym and the bright white interface is killing my eyes. Would love a dark mode that follows system settings. Otherwise very happy as a paid user.

Just started using this and most of the cable and machine exercises I do aren't in the library. Smith machine rows, pec deck, specific leg press variants—all missing. Had to create custom entries and now my history is scattered everywhere.

Returned the app after a week. Syncing workouts between the Watch and phone is completely broken. Sets logged on the Watch either don't show up on my phone for hours or arrive duplicated. As a coach who relies on accurate logs, this is unacceptable.
Wanted to use the Watch app during sessions but it keeps losing connection and dropping sets. Finished a whole workout and only half of it made it to the phone. Not worth the frustration.

The app is fine most of the time, but the rest timer in the background is unreliable. I lock my phone to avoid distractions between sets and the timer just stops. I end up guessing how long I've rested.
Great so far! Only question—is there an Android version coming? My gym buddy wants to use this but he's got a Pixel.
Best app I've used for tracking my team's workouts. Clean, intuitive, does exactly what it should. Highly recommend.
The progress charts are really well done. I can see my volume trending up week to week and spot when I've hit a plateau. Makes it easy to adjust my training.
Spent 10 minutes answering questions and clicking through screens before I could even log my first set. Too much onboarding. Just let me start lifting.
Love the new look after the latest update. Feels snappier and cleaner. Worth the subscription.
The charts are why I pay for SetCount Pro. Seeing my lifts plateau and then break through a PR is so motivating. Great implementation.
Been using Strong for years and switched to IronLog. There's no import feature, so I lost all my history. Really frustrating when you've got thousands of logged sets. CSV import would fix this.
SetCount is solid overall, but the onboarding made me answer 20 questions before I logged anything. Also no way to import my old Hevy data, so I had to start fresh. Would be a 5 if those were easier.

Paid for Pro but I can't log supersets properly. Every time I do a giant set or pairing, the rest timer goes off between movements instead of letting me group them. Makes the paid tier feel incomplete.
Does exactly what I need. Simple, fast, reliable. Switched from a spreadsheet and haven't looked back.
Would love a home screen widget showing my next workout or a rest timer countdown. Live Activities would be perfect too. Keep up the great work.
Finally a tracker that just works. Logging is quick, the interface is clean, no fluff. Really happy with this.
Great for programming, but the exercise library is missing a lot of cable and machine variations I use with clients. Had to add custom entries for half my exercises. Otherwise solid.
At £59 a year, IronLog is pricey, but the plate calculator alone saves me minutes every session. The charts are outstanding too. Worth it for a serious lifter.
Been subscribed for a year and I'm renewing. The progress charts and cloud sync are worth every penny. App keeps getting better.
The free version is decent, but I wish I could import my old Fitbod workouts. Had to re-enter everything manually, which took hours. SetCount got me 90% there though.
The trend lines and estimated 1RM graphs have been game-changing for my training. I can finally see where my peaks and valleys are. Absolutely worth subscribing.
The volume-per-muscle-group chart is fantastic. I was imbalanced and didn't even know it until I saw the data. This app transformed my training.
Paid for a full year and the Watch sync is unreliable. Sets drop, take forever to appear, sometimes duplicate. Feels like a waste when I can't trust the Watch app during sessions.
Good app, but importing from my old tracker was a pain. No CSV support, so I had to manually re-enter a year of workouts. The app itself is solid though.
Subscription is too expensive for what's in the free tier. $49 a year and I'm really just paying for charts and sync that should be standard. Cancelled after two months.
The Watch app crashes constantly and I can't group my supersets. I log a giant set of three exercises and the rest timer fires three times instead of once. Very frustrating for conditioning work.

The plate calculator is a game changer. I used to scribble the loading on my hand between warm-up sets, now I just tap the weight and see exactly which plates go on each side. Worth the subscription alone.

Loved the program structure but the Watch app is letting me down. Sets I log on the Watch show up late or duplicate on my phone, and the rest timer just stops when my screen locks. Defeats the purpose of having it on my wrist.
The Watch integration is broken. Half my workout disappears between the Watch and the phone, and when it does sync the data comes through corrupted or hours late. Switched back to Strong.

Finally can see my actual progress with the trend charts. The 1RM estimate graph is spot on and the volume breakdown by muscle group shows exactly where I'm weak. Love being able to scroll back and see my PR history clearly.
Unusable. The rest timer quits the second I switch to Spotify or check a text. Between sets in a crowded gym I have to keep the phone screen on the whole time. Waste of money.

I was skeptical about paying for a tracker but after using LiftLab for six months I get it. The program templates save me hours designing sessions, the analytics are solid, and the plate math tool alone justifies the cost.
Moving from Strong and there's no import option. I've got two years of lifting history in a CSV and nowhere to load it in. Started fresh but lost all context on my PRs and progression.

Good app overall but my gym just got a new cable station and none of those exercises are in the library. I've had to create five custom entries which is cluttering my history. Wish the exercise list was more complete for specialty equipment.
Really solid app. My only complaint is I wish it had nutrition tracking too but that's outside the scope. Great for logging lifts though.

Imported most of my workouts from a spreadsheet without too much hassle once I mapped the columns right. The process was fiddly and I lost a few entries with bad formatting, but at least the option exists.
I use LiftLab to program for three athletes but I can't push workouts into their apps or see their logs without screenshots and back-and-forth texts. A shared coaching view would save everyone time.

Love the daily readiness checks and the program variety. Wish I could group exercises into supersets though—right now the rest timer fires between every movement instead of between superset pairs. Defeats the purpose of tracking superset density.
Would be great if I could share custom programs with my athletes directly in the app instead of exporting and emailing spreadsheets every time someone wants the template.
Meh.

The Watch app doesn't handle supersets well. I log the first exercise and the timer starts the second. There's no way to tell it 'these two movements are paired' so I'm always fighting the app during giant sets.

Pro version is great for what it does. Exercise library still needs way more cable and machine variations though—hack squat, pec deck, plate-loaded rows. But the superset grouping just got added and it's smooth, love that feature.
Eighty dollars a year is insane for what is essentially a log book. The free tier should include basic charts. Not renewing.

Brought over my Fitbod history through CSV and it mostly worked. A few sets got duplicated and the exercise names didn't match perfectly, but I didn't have to start completely from zero which I appreciated.
Just started lifting and the plate calculator is genius. Before I was guessing, now it tells me which plates for every single rep. Makes warm-up sets fly by.
Best tracker I've tried and the Watch integration is rock solid. Reliable app, clean interface, does everything it promises.
First time using a real training app and the onboarding was painless. Asked what I needed, got me logging in about two minutes flat. Very impressed.
Sat through like twelve setup screens and permission prompts before I could even log a single set. Just let me start lifting. Reinstalled after the first workout because it felt bloated.
Rest timer is completely broken on the paid version. Locks my phone for thirty seconds and the timer vanishes. Music comes on, timer resets. This is the core feature and it doesn't work.
Watch sync is unreliable. Lost entire sessions, sets arriving duplicated hours later, and the Watch app disconnects mid-workout with no way to reconnect. Can't trust it to record my training.
The progress charts are exactly what I needed to see my volume trends over the month. Shows me every lift, every rep, and the estimated 1RM graph is accurate. Worth tracking for the analytics alone.
This plate calculator just saved me so much mental load in the gym. Type in 85kg and instantly know it's two 20s and a 5 per side. Why don't all apps do this.
Tried to import from Hevy and the column mapping was a disaster. Half the exercises didn't import correctly and I gave up and just started fresh. Would have paid extra for reliable import.
The app works well for most exercises but my gym has machines I can't find anywhere—the leg press variants and specific cable stations. Had to create workarounds but overall it's solid.
No way to import from JEFIT even though I used it for three years. Would have switched immediately if I could bring my history. Too annoying to start over so I'm staying put.
The plate calculator feature alone justifies paying for IronLog. Saves me minutes per workout and I never have to second-guess the loading. Best tool in the app by far.

IronLog is fantastic for tracking my athletes' main lifts, but the way it handles supersets is clunky. I have to log each exercise in a separate block, which means the rest timer fires between every movement instead of letting them move through the pair as one unit. Need to group exercises together.

Just switched from pen and paper. The plate calculator is brilliant—no more mental math figuring out which plates go on each side. The $79 annual cost stung at first, but for what I get it's justified.

Loved IronLog until I realised there's no way to import my 18 months of data from Strong. Started fresh today, but I've lost all my history. That's years of progress tracking gone. Not switching again without that option.
Support team helped me reset my password and restore purchases on my new phone in like an hour. SetCount Pro is solid and they stand behind it.
The rest timer doesn't work. Lock my phone and it stops. Switch to Spotify and it resets. I'm paying for a timer that only works if I stare at the screen the whole rest period. Unusable.
The free version is basically useless—charts and sync are locked behind the $49/year paywall. For a tracker app, that's steep. I get more out of Strong and it costs less.
Solid app. One request: a dark mode option. The gym is dark at 5am and IronLog's bright white screen is rough on the eyes. A system-wide dark theme would help.
Really impressed with LiftLab. Picked it up last week and everything just works. Also glad to see kg/lbs labels in my region without hassle—makes a difference.
I love logging my workouts with IronLog but the rest timer has been flaky since the last update. Half the time it doesn't alert me when my phone's locked or in the background. Otherwise great app.

SetCount Pro is not worth $49/year if the rest timer doesn't even work when you're resting. I've missed call-outs, the timer vanishes when another app opens. Completely broken. Switching to something else.

LiftLab costs $59 a year and it's every penny worth it. The structured programs actually kept me consistent, my watch syncs perfectly with my phone, and I can see my progress. Renewing without hesitation.

LiftLab's program library is solid but there's no way to import my old training logs from Hevy. I don't want to lose the history, so I'm stuck maintaining both apps side by side, which defeats the purpose.
Quick setup and the password reset worked instantly when I switched phones. LiftLab made getting started painless.

Paid for the year and regret it. My Apple Watch drops half my sets—sometimes they show up on my phone hours later, sometimes never. Logged a whole workout on the Watch yesterday and only three sets synced. Garbage.
Coach here. I use SetCount with my clients in my region and it's been reliable. Appreciate the language support on the Watch app—makes client setups smooth.
A lock screen widget showing my next workout or rest timer countdown would be perfect. Live Activities during a session would be nice too.
Been at my gym for years and switched to IronLog. Can't import the data from my old spreadsheet or Strong—the CSV import doesn't map the columns right. Frustrating to lose all that history.
Brilliant app, works perfectly on my Watch. Wish there was an Android version so my training partner could use it too, but no complaints about the iOS app itself.
IronLog's charts are really good for spotting plateaus and seeing volume trends. Would be perfect with a dark mode for early morning sessions.
LiftLab's rest timer is completely broken on my Watch. It cuts out or never notifies me, so I'm resting way longer than planned. Wasted money. Worst app experience I've had.
SetCount is okay but the rest timer on the Watch is unreliable. Sometimes it works, sometimes I miss the alert. Not consistent enough for serious training.
The rest timer stops working the second I lock my phone or move to another app. In a busy gym with music playing, I can't rely on SetCount to keep me on schedule. Frustrating.
Had a question about my subscription renewal and the support email came back in a couple hours. No drama, they sorted it out.
The plate calculator in IronLog is genius. Saves me time between sets—just tap it and it tells me exactly what to load. Makes warmups way faster.

SetCount's Watch app looked good but the sets I log there half don't sync back to my phone, and when they do the rest timer between sets doesn't fire at all. It's unreliable for me. I need to log everything on my phone to be safe.
IronLog's interface is crisp and the buttons are huge—easy to tap with sweaty hands between sets. Love the haptic feedback. Real attention to detail.
Commercial gym owner. The plate calculator is a godsend when I'm coaching clients through their lifts. No more confusion about which plates to use. Saves so much time.

I like the progress charts—the 1RM estimates and volume graphs are helpful for planning. Only gripe is the exercise library doesn't have my gym's leg press machine or cable flye variants, so I'm making custom entries that clutter my log.

Logging on my Apple Watch is convenient until I try to rest. The rest timer either vanishes or never alerts me. Defeats the whole purpose of using the Watch version if I can't rely on the timer function.
just started lifting seriously and LiftLab does everything i need. best tracker i've found so far.
Best tracker I've used at my gym. The interface just works, and logging between sets feels natural even when I'm tired.
SetCount is solid but I wish I could share my program with my trainees. Right now I'm screenshotting everything and manually entering their workouts, which defeats the point of paying for this.
Paid for the year and I'm already regretting it. The rest timer constantly dies when my phone locks or a text comes through. I'm timing rests on my watch instead, which is ridiculous.
Great app for tracking lifts, though I'll say the nutrition logging would be nice. Anyway, this does what I need it to.
Love it so far. Do you have an Android version coming? My friend wants to join me but uses Android.
Decent.
I like the Watch app enough to pay for Pro, but forty-nine dollars a year feels steep when the free version already gives me everything I need except the cloud backup. Not sure it's worth renewing.

IronLog is excellent for tracking regular sets, and I love the plate calculator. But there's no superset mode, so I'm logging giant sets as separate blocks and the timer fires between every exercise. Needs a fix.
Brilliant.
The progress charts are fantastic. I can show my clients their estimated 1RM trend lines and they see exactly where they plateaued. Makes programming conversations so much clearer.
The plate calculator is a game changer. No more mental math between sets—just tell me which plates to load and I'm ready. Seriously, this feature alone is worth the subscription.

SetCount Pro is great on my phone, but the Watch app keeps dropping sets. Half my gym sessions arrive late or duplicated on my iPhone, and sometimes the Watch just loses connection mid-workout. Frustrating since I paid for sync.
Support helped me restore my account on my new watch instantly. Really pleased with how fast they got back to me.
Waste of money. The rest timer stops working the second I switch to Spotify or the timer goes into the background. I've missed rest periods countless times. Paid subscribers deserve better than this.
I recommend this to all my athletes. The plate calculator takes the guesswork out of loading, especially when clients ask about switching between kg and lb during a session.
The volume charts and 1RM graphs are really useful for tracking progress. I can see a plateau coming weeks in advance and adjust programming accordingly.
Does exactly what it says on the tin. No bloat, just logging and the tools you actually use.
Good app overall but I'm on the fence about Pro. Free tier already tracks everything, and forty-nine a year for charts and cloud sync feels like a lot for what I use it for.
I switched from Strong and there's no way to import my three years of data. I'm not re-logging 500 workouts by hand. This is a dealbreaker.
The plate calculator is brilliant. Takes seconds to see exactly what to load, and the app handles metric and imperial switches flawlessly. Best part of using this tracker.
The app looks beautiful and the buttons are huge, which is great with sweaty hands, but it crashes every time I open it on my new iPhone. Reinstalled twice, still broken. Can't use it.
Timer is unreliable. Goes into background when I check my form in the mirror or answer a quick message and it either resets or never alerts me. Very annoying after paying for the year.
Missing half the machines at my gym. There's no Smith machine row, no pec deck, no hack squat. I'm stuck making custom entries that clutter my entire history.
SetCount is good but the exercise library is thin. My gym has three different leg press machines and they're all lumped together or missing. I end up creating duplicates just to log accurately.
Won't be renewing. No Android version and my partner can't use this. Also tired of the crashes since iOS 18 beta launched.
I came from Hevy and there's no CSV import option. The app itself is nice, especially on the Watch, but I lost all my old data. Wish I could've brought that history with me.
Do you sell plates with this app? I'm looking for 15kg bumpers and thought this might be the right place.
New update looks slick. Love the cleaner icons.

I use SetCount every day and the rest timer usually works fine, but when I'm doing longer rest periods between heavy singles, the background timer cuts out on me about half the time. Frustrating bug because I paid for reliability, but the rest of the app is solid.
Sixty-nine a year might sound like a lot but the features justify it. I switched from a free tracker and the plate calculator and progress charts have genuinely improved my programming.

I coach five athletes and would love to push programs into IronLog for them to follow. Right now I'm stuck screenshotting everything and emailing spreadsheets. A proper coach-to-athlete sharing feature would make this my go-to app for managing a whole team.

SetCount is solid overall, but my gym has three different leg press machines and a pec deck, none of which are in the exercise library. I've had to make custom entries that clutter everything. Wish the machine library was more thorough.
Just started using this after trying a few others. IronLog is great, does everything I need and the interface is super clean. Very happy.
Five screens asking about my goals, max lifts, experience level, units, rest preferences—before I could even log a single set. Just let me start lifting. Uninstalled.

The progress charts are fantastic. I can see my estimated 1RM climbing week to week, volume trends by muscle group, and exactly when I hit plateaus. Makes it easy to spot what's working. Worth the subscription alone.

Mostly love IronLog, but the Smith machine and cable variations are either missing or buried. I use the Smith press three times a week and end up creating duplicate custom entries that mess up my history.

Absolute waste of money. The rest timer stops working the moment my phone locks or another app comes up. I'll be on Spotify and suddenly no notification that my rest is over. Useless between sets. Returning it.
LiftLab works well for my training, but I'm logging at 5 a.m. in a dark gym and the white screen is blinding. Would really appreciate a dark mode that follows the system setting.
Love it.
Switched from Strong last month and there's no way to import my workout history. Three years of data stuck in another app. Would have stayed if I could just pull it in via CSV.

SetCount Pro costs fifty bucks a year just to unlock charts and sync? The free version already lets you log sets. The app is half-finished without paying, and the rest timer doesn't even work in the background. Not worth $49.

IronLog is very good for most lifts, but cable rows, cable flies, and hack squats aren't in the library. Forced to log them as custom—my workout history is messy now and comparisons across months are useless.
Amazing app. My friends on Android keep asking if there's a version for them. Would love to recommend this to the whole crew but can't until it hits Android.

Been paying for SetCount Pro for six months now. At first I thought £40 a year was steep, but cloud sync and the charts really do tie everything together. Smart investment if you're serious about tracking.
Fifty quid a year for progress charts and cloud sync? The free version logs sets just fine. Way too pricey for what you're paying. Deleted it.

The plate calculator is a lifesaver. I load a barbell at 6 a.m. half asleep and IronLog tells me exactly which plates go on each side for my working weight and warm-ups. Saves me doing the math every set.
I've been a paying subscriber for a year and they just raised the price to $79. For a logging app? I'm out. Great app otherwise, but that's too much.

The Watch app is useless. Rest timer never fires a notification when the phone is locked or when I'm in Music. I'll finish a set and have no idea how long I've rested. Defeats the whole point of using the Watch.

IronLog on the Watch is brilliant. Rest timer goes off right on my wrist even when my phone is in my locker, my log syncs instantly, and the haptic feedback is perfect between sets. Eighty dollars a year is totally worth it for this seamless experience.
The exercise library is small compared to Hevy. Cable variations and different lever machines at my gym aren't there, so I've created a bunch of custom entries. Otherwise it's a nice, clean app.

Love IronLog's charts and plate calculator, but I can't group supersets properly. I log my bench and dumbbell rows as separate blocks and the rest timer fires between every movement, not just between superset pairs. Needs true superset support.
The plate math feature is genius. Loading 100kg per side used to cost me thirty seconds of mental arithmetic—now it's instant. Makes early morning sessions way smoother.

LiftLab is great for following programs, but supersets and circuits feel half-baked. I have to log each movement separately and manage rest timers manually. Would be perfect if I could group them properly.
As a coach, I can't share training programs with my clients inside the app. I'm paying $79 a year and still doing everything via email. Not worth it for me.

My Watch app loses connection mid-session and half my sets don't sync back. Plus the rest timer stops the second the phone locks. Defeats the purpose of having a Watch app.
Dark mode is exactly what the gym needs at 5 AM. App respects the system setting and doesn't drain battery with constant brightness.
The home-screen widget for next workout is super handy. Lock-screen countdown for rest timers would be the perfect next step.
Switched from Hevy and there's no import. Five years of workout history lost because there's no CSV import or any way to bring data in. Frustrating start.
As a coach I wish I could push programs directly into my athletes' apps instead of emailing spreadsheets. Program sharing would cut down so much back-and-forth.
$59 yearly for a program tracker. The free tier does basic logging fine. Overpriced, cancelling my subscription.
Rest timer is completely broken in background. Phone locks, timer resets and never sends the notification. Happens every single session and ruins the flow. Not using this anymore.
Dark mode is a game changer for early sessions. Clean design, big buttons when your hands are wet, and it just works.
App crashes every time I try to log my team's session. Tried on my iPad and iPhone, same issue. Can't use this to coach.
Watch app mostly works but sets sometimes arrive duplicated or way late. Usually fine though, and I love that I can log from my wrist.
Seventy nine dollars a year is too much for this. The free version covers basic logging and that's all most people actually use.
Sets logged on the Watch never arrive on the phone, or arrive three hours later in duplicate. Completely unreliable sync. Defeats the whole purpose.
Crashes on launch every time since I installed iOS 18 beta. Uninstall didn't fix it. My last session is gone. App is broken.
Dark mode is solid. Looks good, doesn't burn your eyes in a dimly lit gym.

Downloaded this after switching to an Apple Watch and the app just crashes instantly on launch since I updated to iOS 18. Tried uninstalling and reinstalling but it won't open. Really disappointed since I wanted to track my workouts on the Watch.
Paid for a year and the app is completely broken. Crashes every time I try to log a set, crashes during workouts, crashes when I open it. This is unacceptable for a paid app.
Just spent $49 on SetCount Pro and it's crashing constantly on my phone at the gym. Sixty dollar app does not work and I can't even use what I paid for. Frustrated.

Love IronLog overall and the interface is slick, but the Watch sync has been dropping sets lately—sometimes I'll log on my Watch and it takes ages to show up on my phone, or doesn't show up at all. Also the rest timer occasionally stops in the background when my music app kicks on. Small issues in an otherwise excellent app.

App keeps crashing whenever I try to finish a workout on my Apple Watch. Manages to sync about half the time, rest of the time I lose the session. 3 stars because it works some days but this is really frustrating.

IronLog was working fine until the iOS 18 beta. Now it crashes every single time I try to open it. Lost my workout data and can't even reinstall it properly. Very disappointed after paying for the subscription.
Finally! SetCount Pro now shows kg and lbs in my regional format. Makes it so much easier logging in my native units without mental conversion. Great to feel heard.

I was hesitant about paying $49 for SetCount Pro but after a month it's absolutely worth it. The free version already tracks sets and reps perfectly, but the charts, cloud backup and Watch app make the paid tier feel like a natural upgrade rather than a money grab.
